question: In the Moshi dialogue setup, what is the frame step size and overall theoretical acoustic latency of the Mimi encoder?
answer: The Mimi encoder processes audio in 80 ms frames, with an overall stride of 80 ms, meaning each latent timestep corresponds to 80 ms of input [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.10 §3.3.1 Architecture (2410.00037v1_3_3_1_Architecture_p10_c025)]. Consequently, the theoretical acoustic latency of the encoder is 80 ms, as the first latent timestep is produced after the first 80 ms of audio has been received [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.10 §3.3.1 Architecture (2410.00037v1_3_3_1_Architecture_p10_c025)].

question: In 'Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling', how does dynamic chunking decide chunk boundaries compared to static chunking?
answer: Dynamic chunking uses a routing module that learns to draw chunk boundaries on the fly, selecting positions that preserve semantically significant tokens while reducing sequence length [arXiv:2507.07955v2 p.3 §1 Introduction (2507.07955v2_1_Introduction_p03_c005)]. In contrast, static chunking applies fixed, predetermined boundaries that do not adapt to the input content [arXiv:2507.07955v2 p.3 §1 Introduction (2507.07955v2_1_Introduction_p03_c005)].

question: In the Moshi dialogue model, which transformer component performs time-series autoregression across frames, and which component models the hierarchical dependency across intra-frame codebooks?
answer: The RQ‑Transformer performs time‑series autoregression across frames, modeling the sequence of RVQ tokens over time [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.26 §5.3 Ablations on generative modeling (2410.00037v1_5_3_Ablations_on_gen_p26_c072)]. The Inner Monologue component models the hierarchical dependency across intra‑frame codebooks, predicting text, semantic, and acoustic tokens in a structured hierarchy [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.26 §5.3 Ablations on generative modeling (2410.00037v1_5_3_Ablations_on_gen_p26_c072)].

question: How does Moshi's multi-stream dialogue architecture differ from prior spoken dialogue systems like dGSLM in terms of text integration?
answer: Moshi’s architecture integrates a text language model backbone (Helium) that is jointly trained with semantic and acoustic token streams, allowing the model to generate text tokens in real time alongside speech tokens [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §2 Related Work (2410.00037v1_2_Related_Work_p06_c013)]. In contrast, dGSLM processes user and system speech as separate audio token streams without incorporating a text language model, limiting its ability to leverage linguistic context [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §2 Related Work (2410.00037v1_2_Related_Work_p06_c013)]. By embedding text generation directly into the multi‑stream Transformer, Moshi can exploit both linguistic and non‑linguistic information during dialogue, whereas prior systems like dGSLM do not [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §2 Related Work (2410.00037v1_2_Related_Work_p06_c013)]. This integration enables Moshi to produce more coherent and contextually appropriate responses in full‑duplex dialogue [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §2 Related Work (2410.00037v1_2_Related_Work_p06_c013)].

question: How does Moshi's multi-stream dialogue architecture differ from prior spoken dialogue systems like dGSLM in terms of text integration?
answer: Moshi’s architecture processes user and system speech as two parallel streams of semantic and acoustic tokens, whereas dGSLM treats them as separate audio token streams in a Siamese setup [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §2 Related Work (2410.00037v1_2_Related_Work_p06_c010)]. Unlike dGSLM, Moshi integrates a text language model (Helium) by generating text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens through its Inner Monologue method, allowing the model to exploit textual knowledge during speech‑to‑speech generation [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.6 §3.1 Overview (2410.00037v1_3_1_Overview_p06_c012)][arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.41 §7 Conclusion (2410.00037v1_7_Conclusion_p41_c092)]. This hierarchical multi‑stream design removes the need for explicit speaker‑turn modeling and enables real‑time, full‑duplex dialogue with text guidance, a capability absent in dGSLM’s pipeline [arXiv:2410.00037v1 p.1 §Abstract (2410.00037v1_Abstract_p01_c002)].
